---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: Profitable Intangible Intensity
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(oiadp, at)), IND_RANK(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), sale)))
HYPOTHESIS: Firms that spend heavily on knowledge and brand building AND still post high operating profitability have an understated asset base, so their measured profitability is a conservative floor on true economic returns and is underpriced.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The product of two industry ranks fires only in the joint corner (high intangible intensity and high profitability), which is exactly the "already-validated" innovator; either theme alone leaves the rank product near the middle. Industry ranking removes sector-level R&D norms so the interaction reflects within-industry differentiation rather than a tech-sector dummy.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: Return On Intangible Capital
EXPRESSION: RATIO(MA(oiadp, 3), ADD(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), COALESCE(intan, 0)))
HYPOTHESIS: Operating income per dollar of accumulated intangible capital (five-year R&D stock plus booked purchased intangibles) measures how productively the invisible asset base converts into profit; high values indicate hidden productive capital the market does not capitalize.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: This is a genuine ratio interaction—profitability numerator over an intangible-capital denominator—so it cannot be replicated by either theme alone; scaling by intangible rather than book capital directly targets the mismeasurement channel. Smoothing income over three years suppresses transitory earnings noise, and the denominator is defined only for firms with some intangible base, restricting the signal to the population the story is about.
INTERACTION_TYPE: ratio

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: Hidden Capital ROA Wedge
EXPRESSION: WINSOR(SUB(RATIO(ib, SUB(at, COALESCE(intan, 0))), RATIO(ib, at)), 1)
HYPOTHESIS: The gap between ROA computed on tangible-only assets and reported ROA equals profitability multiplied by the intangible share of the balance sheet; it measures the dollar magnitude by which conservative accounting understates the earning power per unit of hard capital.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Algebraically the wedge is ib*intan/(at*(at-intan)), a naturally multiplicative profitability-by-intangible-share term rather than a bolted-on composite, and it is zero for pure tangible firms and negative for intangible-heavy loss makers—precisely the desired asymmetry. Winsorizing controls the explosive tail when intangibles approach total assets.
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: Validated R&D Margin Trend
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at), 3)), IND_RANK(TREND(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at), 5)))
HYPOTHESIS: Sustained R&D investment is only informative when it is being validated by an improving gross profitability path; heavy spenders with rising gross profit-to-assets are building real intangible capital, while heavy spenders with flat or falling margins are burning cash.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The interaction is state (R&D intensity level) times slope (five-year gross margin trend), so it identifies innovation that is demonstrably converting into unit economics rather than innovation intensity per se. Investors extrapolate current earnings and underweight the slow-moving trend evidence that intangible spending has begun to pay off.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 5---
NAME: Cash Profitability Of Intangible Firms
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(oancf, at)), INDICATOR(IND_RANK(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), at)), 0.7))
HYPOTHESIS: Cash-based profitability should be far more informative for intangible-intensive firms, whose accrual earnings are mechanically depressed by expensed R&D and advertising, so the profitability premium is concentrated in the top intangible-intensity tercile.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The indicator switches the profitability signal on only where the accounting distortion exists, making the effect explicitly conditional rather than additive; operating cash flow bypasses the expensing bias that makes reported earnings understate intangible-rich firms. Firms outside the intangible group receive zero and sit in the middle of the sort, so the long-short spread is driven by the interaction, not by a generic profitability tilt.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 6---
NAME: Organic Intangibles Profit Gearing
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)), IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(COALESCE(intan, 0), COALESCE(gdwl, 0)), at)))
HYPOTHESIS: Identifiable non-goodwill intangibles (patents, technology, customer lists) represent verifiable productive assets, and when a firm with a large stock of them also earns high gross profitability, the intangibles are demonstrably productive and undervalued; goodwill, by contrast, mostly reflects overpayment and is stripped out.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Separating identifiable intangibles from goodwill isolates asset quality within the recorded intangible base, a distinction that neither a pure profitability nor a pure R&D signal can make. The rank product rewards only firms where booked intangible assets are matched by realized gross profit, filtering out acquisitive balance-sheet inflation.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite
